<description>
`ProcessMessages` takes `cs_main` for every peer on every handler pass, just to check for orphan transactions to reconsider, though most peers have none. This PR checks for orphan work under `m_tx_download_mutex` first and skips `cs_main` when there is none. Peers with orphan work take the same path as before, plus one uncontended lock.

This removes needless `cs_main` contention with validation, RPC and wallet threads. It's part of a broader effort to reduce `cs_main` contention in net processing (see #36244 for context), but stands on its own.

| `ProcessMessages` handling a `ping` | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| no contention | 0.005 ms | 0.005 ms |
| another thread holds `cs_main` for 50 ms | 50.1 ms | 0.02 ms |

Release builds, median of 3 runs. `SendMessages` in the same handler pass still takes `cs_main`.

Tested by `process_messages_without_orphan_work`, which fails without this change.
</description>
